meanings.meaning: Each value, text and membership test reads as the .NET term it stands for, written in the one core's operators under D8.9, as the lambda door reads the same term (spec/Core/translated-members.md). IsNull is eq of the source and null, NotNull is neq: a member the data lacks reads its start first (D4.2), so IsNull holds over one whose start is null, and a value past a holder that holds null reads nothing, so neither IsNull nor NotNull holds over it, as HasValue reads in a list's lambda. IsEmpty over a text is string.IsNullOrEmpty, the nullOrEmpty operator, which holds on nothing, null and the empty text; over a list it is the empty operator, which holds on nothing, null and a list with no item; NotEmpty is not of IsEmpty, so it holds on none of them. Contains, StartsWith and EndsWith compare ordinally, as the lambda door's Contains(string) and StartsWith and EndsWith with StringComparison.Ordinal compare; Matches is Regex.IsMatch over a literal pattern D16.11's reader copies where the view renders (D7.5); MinLength(n) is gte of the text's Length in UTF-16 code units and n, a constant n below zero refused at build and a source n read as .NET reads text.Length >= n. Each text test reads nothing on a text that reads nothing or holds null, and stops its pipeline on a value that is not text. In over literal values is includes of the source in them, each written in the source's form (D8.10), and over a date or a time or of eq of the keys, one term per value, with no value neq of the source's key with itself (D6.12); In over a source that holds a list (N7.3) reads as that list's Any(item => item == value) (D6.2, D8.9), by keys for a date or a time, when the condition runs; NotIn is not of In, and both read nothing on a source that reads nothing; Between(low, high) is gte of low and lte of high, both bounds included, by keys for a date or a time, so it holds over no null. A condition that reads nothing does not hold, so its branch does not run (D8.5).

features.oracle: The C# language specification: an if statement and its else if nesting, the conditional logical operators that read their right operand only when the left does not decide, and the lifted operators over Nullable<T>; .NET's string.IsNullOrEmpty, the ordinal Contains, StartsWith and EndsWith, Regex.IsMatch and String.Length, through spec/Core/translated-members.md; the spec itself for nothing (D8.9), a block's scope (D8.8) and a source's form (D8.10); and for a date or a time, .NET's comparison operators on both hosts and the forms each host writes and binds (D6.12, spec/Core/conversions.md's Keys).

defects.defect: A value test over nothing reads as JavaScript reads it: IsNull holds over a member past a holder that holds null, NotNull holds there too, or IsEmpty does not hold over nothing, so a branch runs that M3.D1 does not run, or the reverse (M3.D1, M3.N1).

A When, ElseIf, And or Or over a source that is no TypedSource<bool> compiles, and the browser tests it by JavaScript's truthiness: N8.2's When and ElseIf take a TypedSource<bool>, and And, Or and Not extend one.
A When given no Then compiles and writes no branch, so its condition is lost without a word: ALIS001, kept and retargeted to the conditions of every block and file (Q18).

A MinLength given a constant below zero compiles, where the redesign refuses it where the view renders: at build by ALIS033's pipeline-condition checks, new:N18.10, and where the view renders on code the analyzer does not follow (D18.6), with the redesign's message, "Condition minimum text length must be zero or greater."

promises.page: A pain meter and a plan text: When the pain is at least 4 the plan reads Call the doctor, ElseIf it is at least 2 the plan reads Give pain relief, Else No action; each branch also writes its own word into a log.
promises.gesture: Set the pain to 5 and click Assess, then set it to 3 and click, then set it to 1 and click.
promises.outcome: The plan reads Call the doctor, then Give pain relief, then No action, and after each click the log holds that branch's word alone: doctor, relief, none.
promises.opposite: At pain 5 the ElseIf's condition holds too, and the log never reads relief after that click.
promises.defect: A later branch whose condition holds runs too, so pain 5 logs relief, or the Else runs after a branch that held, so No action overwrites the plan.

promises.page: A discharge button whose When, the resident's balance equal to 0, holds a {} body of three steps: set the status to Clearing, write Cleared into the log, set the status to Discharged; a step after the branch writes Done.
promises.gesture: Set the balance to 0 and click Discharge.
promises.outcome: The status reads Discharged, the log reads Cleared, and Done shows.
promises.opposite: With a balance of 40 the status keeps Pending, the log stays empty, and Done still shows.
promises.defect: The branch runs one of its steps alone, runs them out of order so the status ends at Clearing, or runs them while its condition does not hold.

promises.page: The resident record's care panel, a ConformanceComponent whose text reads Open and whose Settle() awaits the test app's settle endpoint. A Book button's When, the room free, holds an awaited call to the care panel's Settle() followed by a step that sets the care panel's Text to Reserved, and the step after the branch copies the care panel's text into the summary. The harness gates the settle endpoint (Run.tla's Settle).
promises.gesture: Mark the room free and click Book; once the harness reports the settle held, check the summary, then release it.
promises.outcome: While the settle is held the summary is empty; after the release the summary reads Reserved.
promises.opposite: With the room taken, the summary reads Open at once, with nothing held.
promises.defect: The step after the branch runs before the care panel's Settle() settles, so the summary reads Open, or it waits on a branch not taken, so the summary stays empty.

promises.page: The resident record with a pain box, a number input, and the care panel, the record's ConformanceComponent, whose Check(), a Method<bool> answering its Enabled, true here, adds one to its Calls, which the panel shows; one button's condition is the pain below 4 And Check(), another's the pain at least 4 Or Check().
promises.gesture: Set the pain to 5 and click both buttons, then set it to 1 and click both again.
promises.outcome: At pain 5 the calls read 0 after both clicks; at pain 1 they read 2.
promises.opposite: With Check() read on its own line before the When, the calls rise by one on every click.
promises.defect: The right term is called whatever the left term reads, so the calls read 2 at pain 5, or it is never called, so the calls stay 0 at pain 1.

promises.page: The resident record with a pain meter and the care panel's two ConformanceComponents, nurse and doctor, each showing its calls, the count of its method calls: the nurse's Total() answers its count at once, its Free and Busy buttons setting the count to 1 and 0, and the doctor's SettleCheck() awaits the test app's check endpoint and answers what that endpoint answers. When the pain is at least 8 the plan reads Ambulance, ElseIf the nurse's Total() is above 0 it reads Nurse, ElseIf the doctor's SettleCheck() it reads Doctor, Else Wait. The harness seeds the check endpoint's answer and gates it (Run.tla's Settle).
promises.gesture: Set the pain to 9 and click Assess; set it to 5, click the nurse's Free and Assess; set it to 5, click the nurse's Busy and Assess, and once the harness reports the check endpoint held, check the plan, then release it with the seeded answer yes.
promises.outcome: At 9 the plan reads Ambulance and both calls read 0; with the nurse free it reads Nurse, the nurse's calls 1 and the doctor's 0; with the nurse busy it reads Doctor only after the release, and the doctor's calls read 1.
promises.opposite: With the check endpoint seeded to answer no, the plan reads Wait after the release.
promises.defect: An ElseIf's method runs though a branch before it held, so a calls count rises at pain 9, or the doctor's answer is not awaited, so the plan reads Wait or Doctor before the release.

promises.page: The care panel, the resident record's ConformanceComponent, whose Total(), a Method<int>, answers its Count: Check writes 100 into Count, binds Total(), writes 999 into Count, then When the bound total is below 500 sets the status to Low; Restore writes 600 into Count, binds Total(), and When that total is above 500 its branch writes 999 into Count and then the bound total.
promises.gesture: Click Check, then click Restore.
promises.outcome: After Check the status reads Low and the panel shows the count 999; after Restore it shows the count 600.
promises.opposite: With Check's Total() bound after the write of 999, the status stays empty.
promises.defect: A term or a branch calls Total() again where it reads the bound result, so Check reads 999 and Low never shows, or Restore writes 999 back.

features.summary: The one condition core every condition writes, a pipeline's, a list predicate's and a validator's: the comparisons, the text, membership and value tests, and all, any and not, with one meaning of comparison and logic over null and nothing.
features.oracle: SQL's three-valued logic (ISO/IEC 9075), the truth tables of AND, OR and NOT with unknown, for nothing; the C# language specification's lifted operators over Nullable<T> for null; and spec/Core/translated-members.md for each .NET member a term names.
